decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display draws directly on the firm's core cardboard display know-how. Its absence from the website in 2020–2021 raises some uncertainty, but its own R&D can keep refining it.

The pegboard-back shelf display is a small variation on core competences that design staff can adapt. Not seeing it presented separately suggests it may have been folded into the standard range, so the risk is moderate.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a core format built on existing knowledge and capacity, so it remains worth keeping despite the missing website presence.
The eighth-pallet format extends familiar expertise to smaller placements that retailers still demand. That makes it a sensible keep, with moderate uncertainty.

The technology is familiar, but the media segment is shrinking and the product has gone unobserved since 2019. Releasing its resources to core displays and new development is the better use of the firm's knowledge base.
